media.alt: Worldwide diabetes expected to double in the next 25 years

content.text: "Worldwide diabetes is seen in seven to eight per cent of the population and the number is expected to double over the next 25 years," Dr. Abdul Jabbar, Professor and Head Section of Endocrinology and Diabetes, Department of Medicine at Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH), informed the audience while addressing a public health awareness programme held in Dubai.

Dr Abdul Jabbar underscored the role of intensive lifestyle interventions such as exercise; maintaining a healthy diet and weight; regular blood sugar and cholesterol monitoring; eye and foot examinations; dental and cardiac care; and refraining from smoking or drinking alcoholic beverages in preventing or delaying the onset of diabetes.

He pointed out misunderstandings regarding a 'diabetics' diet,' which are prevalent not only in the general population but also among the health care professionals. He said that patients with diabetes must eat a well balanced diet which will help them control blood sugar as well as help maintain serum cholesterol and lipids levels, thereby minimising the risk of coronary heart disease.

"To help achieve the objective of creating awareness among masses, Aga Khan University Hospital has started a monthly diabetes awareness programme", said Dr Abdul Jabbar. He outlined the necessity and importance of a programme like that by telling the audience that diabetes was a common disorder that was growing at an epidemic rate all over the world. The programme, Healthy People 2000, focuses on helping patients to cope with the implications of this disease, incorporates the need for diabetes education and acknowledges the contribution of education in reducing the morbidity and mortality resulting from diabetes.

Earlier, welcoming the guests, Dr. Rubab Hasan, Patient Referral Coordinator said that AKUH is a philanthropic non-profit institution committed to deliver quality health care to all segments of society. This University Hospital at present offers 500 beds in all subspecialties of medicine, surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology and psychiatry.

AKUH, the principle-teaching site of the Aga Khan University (AKU), is part of Aga Khan Development Network, a group of private international development agencies, founded by His Highness the Aga Khan, which works in the developing countries of Asia and Africa.
AKUH Representative provides convenience and easy accessibility to the Hospital's high-quality, cost-effective services to patients in the United Arab Emirates.

AKUH organises such programmes as part of its outreach programme and societal commitment of creating awareness of early diagnosis and timely treatment. The Hospital has organised over 190 'Signs, Symptoms and Care' programmes in Karachi, Hyderabad and the UAE, benefiting more than 39,000 people. Based on the success of these lectures and in response to the demand for such programmes, this was the eighteenth in the series organised in United Arab Emirates.
The speaker participated in a question and answer session at the end of the programme.
